name: bracket_panel
title: A flat panel of plates, tiles and curved slopes is built lying down and pressed sideways onto outward-facing bracket studs; use it for smooth or sloped vehicle sides, side skirts, cab fairings and box walls.
why: A finished panel built lying down and pressed onto bracket studs: the most-used method in the truck book, for smooth sides of anything.

name: plate_wall
title: Two long plates stacked and stood on edge on a plate with side studs to make a thin strong upright wall; use for slots, cradles and fins.
why: A thin, strong wall from two plates stood on edge, for partitions and thin facades.

name: round_tower_skin
title: Long flat panels of plates topped with curved slopes, mounted sideways on a square side-stud core so it reads as a round tower; use for lighthouses, silos, turrets.
why: A round tower without round parts: curved-slope panels on a side-stud core. For towers, silos, lighthouses.

name: side_stud_column
title: A column or wall corner stacked from bricks with side studs so siding, trim or skin panels can attach sideways later; the base of most SNOT work.
why: A column of bricks with studs on their sides, the core that SNOT details attach to.

name: rounded_corner
title: Shopfront corner post with studs-out core and strips of cheese slopes down both edges, for a softened vertical corner.
why: A softened building corner from slope strips down both edges of a studs-out column.

name: pilaster
title: Masonry bricks and plates stacked lying down with brackets for side studs, then stood up as a stone pilaster or chimney breast.
why: A flat stone pilaster built lying down and stood up, to divide a facade into bays.

name: side_slope_facet
title: A slope pressed onto a side stud so its face points sideways, filling angled gaps or faceting rock faces.
why: A slope pressed onto a side stud to fill an angled gap or facet a rock.

name: snot_end_cap
title: A wall built with forward-facing studs-on-side bricks takes a separately built rounded cap pressed onto those studs, giving a smooth front with rounded corners.
why: A rounded cap pressed onto a wall of forward-facing studs, for the front of a box, a cab, or a wagon.

name: lamp_row
title: A row of round 1x1 lamps sits on forward- or rear-facing studs of a bracket or plate; use it for roof light bars and rear lamp clusters.
why: A row of round lamps on forward-facing studs, for light bars, signal lights, and signs.

name: window_pier_panel
title: A 2-stud-wide wall panel with a 1x2x3 window and side-stud bricks above and below, built standalone so siding, sill and window head can hang on it; use for bay facets or narrow decorated walls.
why: A narrow wall panel with a window, built on its own so trim attaches to its side studs.

name: angled_corner_facade
title: Facade section built on a long wing plate and set across a corner at an angle, one end a round-brick column on a single stud.
why: A facade set across a corner at an angle on a long wing plate, for corner buildings.

name: stone_arched_window
title: Window unit with log-brick stone jambs, a 2x2 grid of frames, a center column and a raised arch head, for grand upper windows.
why: A grand window with stone jambs and an arch head, for town halls and stations.

name: flared_gable
title: A steep flared gable or turret top: side-stud brick columns beside a window carry plates with low slopes, topped by tall 75-degree slopes.
why: A steep flared gable or turret top on side-stud columns beside a window.

name: pent_roof
title: A short sloped roof skirt of 45-degree slopes with convex corner slopes on a plate strip, set on a floor edge to cap a bay or separate floors.
why: A short sloped roof skirt between floors, over a bay or along a facade.

name: flagstone_paving
title: Irregular flagstones from mixed tile sizes and two grays with a few jumpers or bare studs; use for quays, paths and floors.
why: Irregular flagstones from mixed tiles and a few jumpers, for quays, paths, and platforms.

name: modular_joint
title: Technic bricks at the baseplate edge with friction pins sticking out to join the neighboring modular building.
why: Technic bricks and pins at the baseplate edge so buildings join their neighbors.

name: cliff_wall
title: A cliff face of gray bricks whose courses shift in and out, with slope buttresses, sideways facets and a ragged top, built as a panel and attached; use for cliffs and caves.
why: A cliff face from gray bricks whose courses shift in and out, with slope buttresses.

name: rock_spire
title: A tall 75-degree slope capped with a small slope at an odd angle to make a pointed rock; use for any rocky landscape.
why: A pointed rock from a tall slope and a small cap at an odd angle.

name: bracket_stairs
title: Repeating stair step with a riser tile on a bracket, a 2-deep tread and inverted slopes underneath, for straight flights.
why: Stairs from a repeating module with riser tiles on brackets: lighter and smoother than the brick-built stairs we have.

name: drop_in_footprint
title: A tiled ring framing an open studded footprint where a separately built house or tower drops in; use when a model splits into removable modules.
why: A tiled frame around a studded footprint where a separately built building drops in.
